evidence.00504: Sweating, cramps and early diarrhoea during or soon after infusion can be a cholinergic reaction. Tell the nurse immediately. The national regimen says atropine should not be used in patients with glaucoma. Tell the treatment team if you have glaucoma. This source does not give a fixed atropine dose.

additional_support: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prevention is required with this temozolomide regimen. The prescribed medicine helps prevent an opportunistic lung infection; follow its full course and report new cough or breathlessness. Hepatitis B results may require a separate expert prevention and follow-up plan.

Delayed diarrhoea from the earlier irinotecan can continue or start between visits. It can cause dangerous dehydration or infection. Contact oncology at the first loose stool and follow the written anti-diarrhoeal and rehydration prescription. Fever, severe pain, blood, faintness, very little urine or inability to drink needs immediate assessment; never wait for a time threshold when seriously unwell.

Constipation prevention is recommended because vincristine slows the bowel. Antifungal prophylaxis may be considered, but interacting azoles can increase nerve and bowel toxicity and require pharmacy review.

Day 8 contains vincristine only; no scheduled irinotecan or temozolomide dose. Delayed diarrhoea from the earlier irinotecan can still occur; continue prescribed infection prevention and other support.
Follow the current prescription; an improved test result does not authorise restarting after a hold.

guidance.label: Current national regimen and reconciled local prescription

evidence.00504: The treatment service chooses suitable intravenous access. Report burning, pain, swelling or redness during administration immediately. If a port or central catheter is used, agree dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Do not alter infusion settings yourself. Keep temozolomide in its supplied packaging; do not crush or open capsules. Ask the pharmacy how carers should handle the medicine and what to do after a damaged capsule or spill.

closures.evidence: Irinotecan 50 mg/m² is given intravenously on days 1–5 of each 21-day cycle. Temozolomide is taken by mouth on days 1–5: 125 mg/m² in cycle 1. Only the treating team may select 150 mg/m² from cycle 2 after toxicity review. Vincristine 1.5 mg/m², maximum 2 mg, is given on days 1 and 8. The national plan specifies 12 cycles unless progression, toxicity or the specialist plan changes treatment. Take temozolomide fasting, swallowed whole with water, at least one hour before irinotecan. If you vomit after temozolomide, do not take an extra dose.
